My name is Elizabeth, and when I was in Class 4, my friend Hrithik's mother died. When he came back to school, nobody knew what to say, so nobody said anything. He sat alone at lunch.
I didn't know what to say either. So I sat next to him and opened my tiffin. I had idli. I pushed one towards him. He took it.
The next day I brought my comic book and we read it together, not talking. The day after, we played hopscotch.

I don't think I said anything clever. But he told me, years later, that the hopscotch was the first time he laughed after.

Noor came back to school today, two weeks after her mother's death. She was quiet at assembly and sat very still in class. At break she stayed at her desk.

Sarika came back to school today after her Nanaji's funeral. At lunch, Mehul said to her, "Well, at least your Nanaji was really old. He had a good long innings." He meant it kindly, I think. Then Tanya added, "Everything is part of God's plan."

The whole Class 11 of the small-town school went to Ojas's house after his father's funeral. They sat on durries in the courtyard, uneasy.
Baljeet watched as Harpal patted Ojas's shoulder and said, "Everything is God's will, yaar. He's in a better place now." Another boy added, "At least you have your mother."
Ojas nodded, but his hands were clenched on his knees, and he stared at the ground.
Baljeet felt his stomach turn. The words sounded right, but Ojas looked like he'd been hit.

"I know," Baljeet said. They sat until the lamps were lit.

The day Sudha's mother died, Gopika came before sunrise with a big pot of rice and dal, because she knew no fire would be lit in that village house. She said nothing much. She swept the courtyard and sat at the edge of the mat while women wept inside.
Sudha sat numb. Gopika didn't tell her to be strong. She just stayed, filling water pots, handing her a glass now and then.
The relatives left after the thirteenth day. The house fell silent.

Three months after her father's death, Zainab went back to teaching at the small-town girls' school. To everyone who asked, she said, "I'm fine, Allah's will." She smiled at the staffroom, graded papers, ate lunch alone.
At night she lay awake, feeling nothing at all, and then suddenly furious at the ceiling fan, the neighbours' radio, everything.

"Tell me about him," Uma said.
